I am 24 years old and went with my mom and the environment fit any type of group: family with small children or a younger crowd with friends. Overall a great trip and highly recommended. I want to go back already!

-Sepi & Sami

reviews.author: Rod T
reviews.title: Ooo LaLa
reviews.text: By far the best all-inclusive resorted out of three that we have visited.  Paradisus got it right! From reception to checkout our experience was fantastic.  We booked this last minute trip while visiting family in Dominican Republic. We elected for the Royal Service package that included our very own butler (Alvaro). To reach the butler, Paradisus give you a cell phone so you can contact your butler 24/7 for everything from reservations to excursions or just for general information. Alvaro walked us to our room and made sure everything was fully functional and to our liking. He also gave us the grand tour the next morning and gave us some suggestions on where to eat and what to do. Our room was very nice, king size bed, pillow menu from hard to soft and a few scent options. Jacuzzi in the room was hot and ready for us with rose pedals and a bottle of champagne. Everyone at the resort were genuinely nice and attentive. Shout outs to Gladys Morla and Stephanie Auguste who greeted us and provided exceptional service at the restaurants on a daily basis.   Also to Chef Carlos Seuno at Plazzo Resturant, the food was terrific. Thanks for allowing us to sample your test menu items. Our beachside bartender Jorge Acevedo was funny and always keep our cups full.  We also had good seafood at Gabi Beach. The shrimp and fish was tasty. The Market Grill was good for breakfast but we enjoyed Plazzo better because of the made to order pancakes :-). Another great mention to Isabel Reynos. Thanks for making us feel special. Thanks to Maria at the spa, the couples massage was great. Thanks to your co-worker, sorry we forgot her name. Also thanks to the spa manager for tailoring our spa package to exactly what we wanted. Your patience with us is appreciated :-).  We had dinner one night at The Reserve, a sister resort just a couple min cart ride from our resort. We ate at the Mizu, Oli Cruz and Octavino Liranzo served up good food and even better service; these two knew how to work the diverse crowd and make everyone feel special. Thanks guys. The complimentary water activities were an added bonus. We took advantage of the kayaking and loved it. We also enjoyed the Michael Jackson tribute concert.

reviews.author: Kim M
reviews.title: Excellent vacation
reviews.text: The resort is five star! It's located on the most beautiful private beach with plenty of excellent restaurants the Italian being my favorite. The pools are amazing, the people are friendly, we had our own butler "Samuel " who took great care of us bring us special treats to the room. We did yoga everyday and had the most amazing yoga instructor "Angela Guzman".  The golf course was nice. There were lots of extras that made the trip we had fresh coconut water by the pool, fresh juice bar by beach cabanas  "George Acevedo" took very good care of us! They had night life casinos, shows, dancing. And the spa was amazing!

reviews.author: amijaresgil@yahoo.es
reviews.title: mi experiencia en mis 70 años
reviews.text: Disfrutamos del Royal Service.  El Paradisus ya lo conocíamos con anterioridad, ahora se encuentra muy mejorado gracias al mantenimiento y a las maravillosas atenciones que nos bridaron todo el personal.  Nuestro mayordomo fue ALVARO FERNANDEZ, quien con un gran profesionalismo y atenciones de primera nos permitió pasar unos días inolvidables. Estimo que ALVARO merece todo el aprecio y reconocimiento de todos.  En mis cumple 70 hasta me organizó todo un día de actividades increíbles, incluyendo el arreglo de nuestro yacuzzi. Muchas gracias. Igualmente vale la pena señalar la excelente atención y cordialidad de Francisco, el mesonero de la playa, el chef del Rest. Palazzo, Carlos Díaz es uno de los mejores que he conocido preparándonos platos que le sugeríamos desde el día anterior, recomendable, al igual que la anfitriona del Palazzo y los mesoneros. Gracias a todos,,,,volveremos pronto..a mijares gil

reviews.author: Emily080
reviews.title: Not perfect and my needs were simple.....
reviews.text:
My daughter and I stayed in this resort from Sept 2 -9, 2014.  On arrival, we were offered an upgrade to Royal Service for a substantial additional charge (1/3 of the price we paid for the entire trip).  Since we arrived at off-season we declined.  Then I found out that the room reserved for us only had 1 bed.  Looking for another room with 2 beds seemed to be a big problem for them.  As a result, check-in took over 30 minutes.  Then we were told that our room wouldn't be ready for another 30 minutes, so we walked around the resort.  We arrived around 2:25 pm and did not get into our room until 3:50 pm. 

The room we were assigned was on ground floor, close to the Flamingo pond.  Although the room was dated, smelled musty, had bad shower, too-soft-mattresses and pillows with poor support, it was conveniently located close to the gym, lobby lounge, business centre and all restaurants.  So we decided to stay in this room for the rest of our stay. 

Tourist card/Departure tax – Most airlines from N. America (except Sun wing) include these in their ticket price.  If you were given a Tourist Card at the Airline check-in counter, then the departure tax would also be included.  Keep the Tourist card given to you.  You have to give this card to the official on arrival.  Don’t lose it or you would have to line up in Punta Cana Airport and paid another US$10/pp.

West Jet - This airline does not have web check-in in Punta Cana.  If you call them within 24 hours of your flight, they may reserve your seats for you but you still need to check-in.

Dinner Reservation System – as posted by other tourists, this is a frustrating process.  When you reserved your dining table with the Guest Service/Concierge, you apparently are only leaving a “request”.  Your table is not confirmed until around 5:30 pm the day of.  Very often, the time you asked for would be changed.  In our case we booked the Teppanyaki table one night for 6:00 pm.  We received no confirmation note so we walked up there anyway, just to find out that our reservation had been changed to 8:30 pm.  No one advised us of the change.  The restaurant was empty, with couple of chefs standing around but no guest!  No reason was given why they could not accommodate us at 6 pm.

The Beach – Very nice cabanas set up all over the beach and pool area.  The ground was beautiful. Unfortunately, the beach was loaded with seaweeds (see my picture).  I ventured in just to find myself wrapped in seaweeds: on my chest, around my waists and ankles.  That was very unpleasant so I never went back to the ocean again.  

Loud music around the pool – one couple plugged their ipod to a portable speaker and turned the volume real loud while they floated around the pool.  We only saw them once.  The worst offender was actually the exercise instructor in the resort.  He worked out with one or two clients by the pool.  He has a 3 feet tall speaker blasting out his R&R music in full force.  We could hear his music all the way down the beach.  We did not go there to listen to his music and there was no need to be that loud.  His clients were right next to him.  I found that very annoying.

The Beach attendants – They fetched our drinks and worked diligently on the beach; rain or shine.  We were well attended to.  Their service was exceptional, especially Georges Alriche who was polite, non-intrusive and fast.  He checked on us at reasonable time intervals just to make sure that we were OK.  He made our stay on the beach very pleasant.

Food – I never encountered the F&B Manager in the 7 days we were there.  Generally speaking food was bland, unimpressive but there were some good meals and no MSG.   
Bana – avoid that place if you could.  Breakfast and lunch buffets were the worst I had ever seen in a resort.  Sushi was awful (stale fish on thick roll of rice); Sashimi was disgusting.  California Rolls had no avocado but thick chunk of hard cream cheese.  To make it worse our server doesn't speak English.  The only food I liked from this Dining Room was the Oatmeal, steamed potatoes, walnuts and the tiramisu squares which were only available the first 2 days of our stay. 
Vento – This is the shining star: Manager was visible and readily available. It has a warm cozy ambiance.  For the first time we found some soft buns, not the recycled hard dinner rolls we saw over and over again during breakfast.  All meals served were tasty and well presented.
Passion – This is a specialty restaurant with charges (US$60/pp) – It has very nice décor and good meal.  We ordered a la carte but were still given a lot of “samplers” to taste.  My filet mignon was very tender but unfortunately slightly under-cooked.  It’s worth the try to get that one special meal.
Market Grill – This is a convenient place to drop by for a quick afternoon snack.  Nothing outstanding from here; this is an open-sides restaurant by ocean front.  A cover-up over your bathing suits is adequate.

Were there melted cheese and flies?  Yes, I saw them as well.  The cheese was melted, corners all dry, and occasional flies landed on them.  Tiny sandwiches were made in hard crusty rolls and they looked recycled.  No one picked them up.  They were served in Bana & Market Grill.

Room Comfort – Beds and pillows were too soft, limited privacy since the bathroom was separated from the bedroom by shutters only, then lined with wood slates on both sides.  You would be clearly visible inside your bathroom so don’t order room service until you are all done with the bathroom.  Shower did not have good pressure.  The room was spacious though very dated.

Communication – Front Desk, Concierge, and Guest Service has English speaking staff.  In the restaurants, servers have very limited English.  Coffee cream and milk to them are the same.  The 3 PCs in Business Centre are in Spanish, only one PC could be switched to English through the Control Panel.

In Summary, this resort is clean, well maintained and staff tried to make things right for me every time.  Stephanie in Guest Service went out of her way to do a Web check-in for me.  Services otherwise were sporadic.  For example, some days I had Housekeeping knocking on my door at 8:40 am and wanted to clean our room.  Some days they did not show up the whole day and I had to call.  Bar fridge were stocked one day and not the next.  We constantly ran out of bottle water.  Dinner reservation was a guessing game: Are we dining at  6 pm, 6:30 pm, 7 pm or 8:30 pm?  We did not know for sure until after 5:30 pm.

During the last few days of our stay, the resort was deserted.  A huge Tropical Storm on Monday’s early morning caused the sewage system somewhere to overflow later in the day.  The Resort smelled absolutely foul which was very unfortunate for new arrivals.  The ground and pool were really nice.  Maybe if you opt for Royal Service, your room maybe better.  If you want to do so, booked this through your agent or on line, don’t do it when you are already on site.  That would cost A LOT MORE. 

My needs are simple: clean quiet beach, quiet space where I could read, good food, comfortable bed and good shower.  No matter where I went, I found loud music: by the pool, on the beach, in the Gym.  The worst of course was the seaweeds on the beach and in the ocean.

reviews.author: Gabsantanadiaz
reviews.title: Un Sueño...
reviews.text: Desde que llegué me sentí como una reina. Muy buenas atenciones! Un equipo de animación espectacular, Rafael siempre nos encontró una actividad nueva y entretenida, Gracias! El equipo de Grupos es muy atento, especialmente Yohanna Genao, quien estuvo pendiente de que todo saliera bien durante nuestra estadía. Los camareros del Gabi Club son muy atentos también. Por favor, procuren ir a la fiesta de la playa que hacen los sabados, eso no tiene comparación! Es sin duda lo que mas disfruté. En fin, desde el principio hasta el final de mi estadía todo el mundo fue muy atento. Pronto volveré asi que espero que sigan con ese excelentisimo servicio.

reviews.author: parman23
reviews.title: Jack hammer and constuction noise all day
reviews.text: This resort does not like Americans  we stayed had a party of seven of us, trip booked by Liberty Travel,  Construction at resort all day long JACK HAMMERING BREAKING CONCRETE, all you hear at pool or beach , service was terrible. all inclusive they beg you for TIPS if you do not give it to them they ignore when you want your next drink, Package  had extras we never received, Liberty Travel did nothing to help us. Hotel manager told us you are not in the united states ,You are in in  foreign country  live with the problems you are going home soon, too bad for you, did not want to fix problems,  restaurants over crowded, long lines to eat,  told premium drinks did not have premium booze, Hotel rooms no face cloths, no hot water in shower, bathroom sink glogged  when you brush your teeth. Water sports include they would not let you use them, STAY AWAY FROM THIS PLACE TERRIBLE

reviews.author: Bola S
reviews.title: A wonderful relaxing family holiday
reviews.text:
My 11 year old son & I stayed at the Reserve from 8th Aug to 22nd Aug 2014. Right from before we arrived it was just going to be wonderful. This is my 4th trip to Punta Cana always staying at one of the Melia Group and this is the second time at a Reserve. This Reserve (Paradisus Punta Cana) was by far the best stay.
Silvio Lantigua helped me out with decisions long before I arrived - making sure that everything was set up for us after a 17 hour journey. Silvio I thank you again!
Johana at reception thought it might be a good idea to upgrade to the Family Concierge & it was a great idea! My son really appreciated it. My main concierge was the lovely Sofia and when she wasn't there Leidy took over seamlessly. I cannot express my gratitude more to these two lovely ladies who made our stay so effortless. And yes - anything you want - can be arranged. Apart from the restaurants - bug spray, packing material , pumping up pool toys - anything! And with a smile and willingly. It really made our stay so much more enjoyable.

At the reserve pool, we were so well looked after by Emilio Valdez, Jose delo Santos and Santos. They worked tirelessly with humour and charm!
My son could never wait until the Hydro Grlll opened every day and made sure he sampled all the menu; becoming great friends with the two Chefs who served us.

Jose in activities was great - but everyone probably agrees that Ruben Dario Castillo kept this place pumping. With a smile, with activities, with conversation for both kids and adults. What a star. I cannot list all the activities that were organised needless to say that in the 2 weeks we were there; we took part in something every single day, most of which were led by Ruben.
And a big shout out to the Head of Activities - who helped with set-ups and once it was dusk; he did his best to ensure that everyone (young & old) had a great time partying in all parts of the hotel. A very good effort especially after working in the sun all day long!

There was so much for my son to do & thanks to the activity guys Pedro Aquino and Jose dela Cruz; I could relax whilst he bungee jumped, wall climbed or did archery with the guys. The whole place was so  safe that I did not have to worry at all.

Alongside beautiful grounds, our comfortable & spacious room, we also took in a few days at the  Beach where Mikey and Luis worked hard in the sun to keep everyone happy. It made the experience so much more laid back.

Lots of different restaurants to choose from, but our favourite was The Grill in the evening. And there Angel the Sommelier explained the finer points of the wines on offer which the hotel credits make very affordable and will store for you; to be ordered at your next meal if you are the only one drinking it in your party. What a great idea!

The evening entertainment was fun for both kids and adults and just long enough to keep the little ones involved. 

Two weeks really wasn't enough, The Reserve Paradisus Punta Cana gave us a wonderful holiday and we're counting the months until we can make a return trip all the way from ..... Dubai, UAE!!!

reviews.author: Yazan S
reviews.title: Needs work
reviews.text: We enjoyed our stay and had many things to do. Food was good but service to room was slow . Most employees don't speak fluent English which was very frustrating . Our bed and sofa were extremely uncomfortable  . They also need better musquito control.

reviews.author: Marcelo0712
reviews.title: Tudo o que se espera de um Hotel
reviews.text: Desde a recepção, percebe-se que  são pessoas extremamente profissionais e competentes pata lidar com o turista. Uma férias sem se preocupar com nada, camareiras atenciosas, garçons excelentes e tudo avança numa perfeita harmonia neste hotel.

reviews.author: anoblett
reviews.title: Birthday Trip w Friends and Family
reviews.text:
Great trip......great service, food, cocktails, spa/ resort and great memories! !!!!
If you do the royal service,which I highly recommend, ask for Sandy. Sandy, our group butler, went the extra mile for our rather large group. He never said no. Managed do all behind the scenes w a smile on his face all the time. When things weren't working out (like our transfer to the airport going home) he drove us himself...pretty sure that wasn't on his job title.  He had such the right temperament with a sweet sense of humor.  You could tell he enjoyed his job.
Leonardo Moto, the adult pool bar bartender in Royal Service, was attentive and remembered everyone's name.  Be careful though...he is a heck of a connect four player.  Had a crowd gathered just to see if one of the guest could beat him...happy to report my hubby was the only one THAT day.
Omar, took great care of us each day poolside to make sure our day was all set prior to stepping outside. Checking w us frequently to make sure our needs were met.  He was very friendly and had a warm smile...nice to see each day.   Highly recommend staying here if you want a trip to remember while staying in the Dominican Replublic.

reviews.author: Gladys G
reviews.title: entretenido
reviews.text:
Nos quedamos en Royal Service, donde nuestro mayordomo estuvo siempre preocupado por nosotros, me refiero a Evian, quien también nos sorprendió con un Jacuzzi, se preocupó ademas de las reservas a los restaurantes.  También nuestros agradecimientos a Leonardo Mota y a Antonio de los bares, quienes siempre atendían con una sonrisa y muy buena disposición. Mencionar también a los amables camareros del Palazzo y los otros restaurantes, quienes siempre lo hacían con mucho agrado, y a la recepcionista Stephania.
Las habitaciones muy buenas, sólo reclamar por el wifi, que costaba mucho que se conectara.
Además a pesar que pagamos más por Royal Service, el vino era en todos los restaurantes el mismo, a no ser que uno cancelara por otro mejor aparte. Mencionar también a Angel quien era el encargado de la entretención, quien siempre hacía lo que estaba a su alcance para entretener a los huéspedes,  Muy buenos los show.
En general nuestra estadía fue muy buena, lo pasamos muy bien .

reviews.author: Amanda R
reviews.title: Honeymoon
reviews.text: This place was great from the moment we got here. We ended up upgrading to the royal services and so glad we did. There are more restaurants and premier liquor that was worth it. We were also assigned a butler and he was awesome his name was Eviån Rodriguez, as for him. He made all the dinner reservations for the week and for the most part they were all great. The royal service also comes with a private pool and bar area. The bartender there was also and his name was `Leyo moyor I think. I will say there are private cabanas that were awesome but we were never able to get one not sure why, we had asked several times but nothing. They said the hotel was not full but anyways the pool was still great. The staff was very nice and attentive and dinner was always never nice. I will say in general if you have any stomach issues or sensitive make sure to bring a lot of meds. We had several days my husband and I did not feel great not sure what is was but apparently that is common when eating food from other countries. The room was great and very clean and also put back together when we would leave. All and all it was a great vaca and would go to another paradisus else where.

reviews.author: JZee
reviews.title: oustanding resort.......
reviews.text: I must say that this resort is outstanding for the service, cleanliness, grounds, entertainment, staff always finding ways to satisfy you and go out of there way, food a la carte and buffet really good...........a recommended place for vacation.

reviews.author: Ovi10
reviews.title: Vamos a volver
reviews.text:
El hotel es imprescionante,  las habitaciones para el servicio Real valen la pena,  picina privada, y playa con poltronas comodisimas y servicio de playa excelente.
El servicio  de mayordomo, es fundamental, ya que te olvidas de reservar resto u organizar tu noche , elegis le avisas y el hace vos solo disfrutas
Tiene deportes acuaticos sin motor free son divertidos! y las excursiones salen desde el hotel o desde la playa!
extraño este lugar! queremos volver ya!

reviews.author: ElizabethE0215
reviews.title: Wonderful week in a gorgeous location!
reviews.text:
Our trip to Paradisus Palma Real was wonderful. We stayed in an ocean view Royal Service suite, which I highly recommend. Royal Service includes a private check in/check out process, private pool and beach areas and butler service. Our butler, Juan, was great. He set up all of our dinner reservations, reserved us a palapa by the private pool and left surprise amenities in our room each evening, including cheese platters, chocolate covered strawberries, champagne; and of course preparing our whirlpool tub with bubbles and candles. Royal Service also includes access to the Royal Service lounge, with premium liquors, wines and a small buffet of snacks. We usually visited there before dinner for a drink and appetizers. 

The food was very good at all restaurants. Breakfast at Palazzo can be buffet or menu. The menu is limited, but good. The buffet is small, but also good. You can also have French toast, crepes, pancakes or eggs made at the griddle station. Breakfast at Bano is all buffet and much more extensive than Palazzo.  Benefit of Palazzo is the outdoor seating overlooking the main pool. Very pretty. 

For lunch you can do buffet at several places, the two mentioned above or at Market Grill. Or go to Gabi Beach and order from the menu. I preferred Gabi Beach - again the open air atmosphere overlooking the beach really made the difference for me. 

Dinner - the good: Market Grill (excellent lobster and steak), Gabi Beach (awesome seafood selections and a great lamb dish), Palazzo (excellent everything). The "eh": Bano has a Japanese steakhouse that just wasn't great. If you go there maybe try the sushi bar or the other side of the restaurant where they have Thai. 

We didn't try Vento or Passion. And Nano was closed during our trip. 

I only have a few small (very small) complaints - they really want you to join Club Melia and will do a push for you to spend 45 minutes getting the presentation. We managed to skip it, but got a minor guilt trip for it (just some sad eyes and disappointment). And when we were there the WiFi was out everywhere except the Royal Service lounge for the first couple of days - but no one had any info about it. Finally our butler found out and let us know.  Room service is limited, but good when it arrives (our breakfast on the last day was about 15 minutes late). And lastly, the phone in our room kept ringing (loudly) at odd times and when we would answer the caller didn't speak any English, would hang up and we never found out what that was about. It may have been another guest trying to reach a different room. Was just a bit annoying. 

We definitely will visit this resort again. The entire experience was excellent.

reviews.author: Manuel Efren G
reviews.title: Todo lo que puedas esperar y más...
reviews.text: Pasamos 8 días en familia espectaculares, donde la diferencia estuvo en la calidad de servicio, las instalaciones son bellísimas y muy bien cuidadas pero la diferencia está en su gente...los muchachos del Gaby club son excelentes Luis Vásquez, Georibel Guzmán, Frank Martínez, Elisaul Cedano cuidando cada detalle del servicio, Teuris siempre pendiente de que nos sintiéramos bien, Janna y sus atenciones con nuestros niños, Diosmery Francisco en el Family Concierge, Arturo de los Santos por sus atenciones en Mole y The Grill y Lilian Jiménez en Fuego...Ramón por su servicio en el bar de la playa y Rodolfo y Jorge del North Avenue Bar...las muchachas del kids zone, se nos escapan algunos nombres, realmente desde que llegamos hasta nuestra salida nos sentimos cuidados y atendidos con esmero...fue una excelente elección!!

reviews.author: Gypsy M
reviews.title: EXTRAORDINARY VACATIONS!!!!!
reviews.text: Every year that we go to Punta Cana for our family vacation is fenomenal. We always stay at the Reserve Area and the employees are ALWAYS dedicated and taking care of us. Mr.Silvio Lantigua loves what he does and you can tell in the way he treats the guests. Also, Ruben Dario, Emilio Valdes, Yadilky Mercedes are very professional and always with a smile for everybody. Good experience every time that we go. Highly recommended.

reviews.author: Bnv
reviews.title: lua de mel
reviews.text: Hotel bem estruturado, em bom estado e com bons serviços. Perfeito para ocasião, nos proporcionou uma belíssima estada e romantismo. Comida de qualidade no restaurante Palazzo, no estilo bistro e bebidas premium no lounge bar do Royal Service. Se vcc deseja um atendimento diferenciado, exclusividade e qualidade não abra mão de se hospedar no Royal Service. YHA SPA um show a parte, estrutura estupenda, atendimento sensacional em um ambiente digno de 5 estrelas. Voltaria e indicaria a opção do Royal Service. Tivemos uma experiência muito positiva.

reviews.author: Jorge_Berlin
reviews.title: Immaculate vacation
reviews.text: Immaculate vacation. Royal Service with our personal Butler Samuel Rodriguez was worth every penny. Fast, reliable and efficent service delivered to your doorstep when you needed it. May it be reservation for booked out restaurants, repair of a faulty sewer pipe which disturbed our sleep for one night, ironing of shirts in unbelievable quickness, he allways made the impossible possible. Service delivered like to a friend. Really enjoyed it. Nothing to complain besides maybe the fact that they have to work on their WiFi. Bad reception in a lot of areas. That was maybe the only downside. If you want to pamper yourself with a luxury vacation, here it is.

reviews.author: MiguelLazcano
reviews.title: Excelente servicio
reviews.text:
No nos queda mas que agradecer el maravilloso servicio que nos han otorgado por parte del personal de Paradisus Palma Real Resort.
Destacar la labor y buena atencion de Leonardo Mota, del bar de la piscina del Royal Service, que dia a dia nos atendia con simpatia y excelentes servicios.
Destacar tambien la atencion completa del restaurant PALLAZO, en especial de la anfitriona de los desayunos, que lamentablemente no recuerdo su nombre , pero que siempre se preocupo de darnos una muy buena atencion y una calida bienvenida, lo que hizo que ese restaurant se convirtiera en nuestro favorito.
Solo decir dos cosas que nos complicaron, la conexion a internet que ni en el Royal Service funcionaba correctamente y lo segundo, que en la entrada del resort, donde te dejan los taxis, no existe una rampla para personas discapacitadas,  para descender de estos.

Reitero los agradecimientos por el excelente servicio entregado por todo el personal y espero volver muy pronto para vivir nuevamente la experiencia Paradisus Palma Real Resort.

*Lamento la falta de tildes, pero los computadores del resort estan desconfigurados.

reviews.author: rachralin
reviews.title: Mais do que perfeito! Inigualável!
reviews.text:
Passamos os últimos 6 dias da nossa lua mel no Paradisus Palma Real e posso dizer que foram dias mais do que perfeitos. Superou as minhas expectativas - que já eram altas por causa dos reviews que tinha lido. Tive o maior cuidado em selecionar um hotel que tivesse condições de deixar ainda mais inequecível nosso lua de mel. E posso dizer que o hotel atendeu e muito nossos anseios.
Ficamos numa suíte com vista mar com Royal Service, o que foi perfeito! A acomodação era espaçosa, com banheira de hidromassagem no quarto. O banheiro e o quarto são conjugados, com ventanas que permitem deixar comunicáveis os dois espaços.

A comida era simplesmente perfeita! Pratos deliciosos do Gabi Beach, como o carpaccio de peixe branco delicioso que comemos!  O Palazzo - restaurante exclusivo do royal service - tem uma comida maginífica e supreendente, onde lagostas e camorões são servidos abundantemente. Para ter noção da variedade e supreendente culinária, vale citar a existência de caviar no café da manhã do Palazzo. O tepannyaki é um restaurante igualmente delicioso em que o chefe prepara os pratos na chapa na sua frente e dos demais hospédes que dividam a mesma ilha. Todos os restaurantes que comemos, mesmo no estilo buffet, apresentaram alta qualidade e sabor.
O Passion - restaurante que não faz parte do all inclusive - vale muito a pena a visita, sendo uma experiência inesquecível com pratos exóticos mas maravilhosamente deliciosos! Além de contar com uma equipe sensacional, que torna ainda mais surpreendente e positiva a experiência! Optamos pelo o menu tasting e foi divino! O emparelhamento de vinhos também perfeito (pago a parte)!

Ficamos deslumbrados ainda com os funcionários e os serviços do hotel! Pessoas muito simpáticas que sempre mostravam cordialidade e prestavam serviço 5 estrelas, deixando ainda mais prazerosa nossa estadia. Não podemos deixar de citar, assim, nosso butler chiquérrimo e ótimo SANDY GRILL, que fez questão de atender nossos anseios, providenciando nossas reservas e mimos inesquecíveis. Muito obrigada!
Além disso, José Matteo no Gabi Beach, com excelente serviço e atendimento, sugerindo drinks e pratos deliciosos!
OMAR da praia.. providenciando as toalhas, os drinks, os cuidados.. com um astral excelente!
Leonardo Motta do bar da piscina do royal service que faz, com uma tremenda animação, os melhores drinks, inclusive a perfeita margarita frozen!
O resort é sensacional! Já nos hospedamos em outros resorts all inclusive, no litoral do nordeste e outros na republica dominicana, mas este resort mudou complemente minha perspectiva!
É simplesmente SENSACIONAL!

reviews.author: Carlos H
reviews.title: Vacaciones en The Reserve Paradisus Punta Cana
reviews.text: No tengo palabras para describir lo excelente que es este hotel en todos los aspectos, el servicio ni se diga especialmente de parte de la Gerente de The Reserve, la Sra. Kristhel y todo su equipo de trabajo incluyendo tambien al Sr. Silvio Lantigua que mas amable no pueden ser. Le recomiendo este hotel a todo el mundo 100% en TODO.!!!!!!!

reviews.author: 220beverlyk
reviews.title: Wonderful, relaxing time in paradise
reviews.text: This was a first time for my daughter and I to take an all inclusive vacation to a tropical location. We went to celebrate her 30th birthday. We could not have chosen a more beautiful location and a great service hotel.  Gregorio Guillen was a wonderful wait staff - so friendly and enjoyed trying to teach us the language.  We also enjoyed Carlos, Rodney and Mario - they all went out of their way to be courteous and friendly.  I would recommend the Paradisus Palma Real to anyone who is looking to take a paradise vacation.

reviews.author: Kim J
reviews.title: Great place!
reviews.text: We have been to many all inclusive and found this place to be one of our favorites. We did upgrade to the Royal service which we were glad we did. Our butler Juan De Leon... Was EXCELLENT! He along with Martin were the best!!!! With the royal upgrade we enjoyed a private pool, a butler, a restaurant and lounge. Evian was our butler for the first part of our stay and he did a nice job showing us around and explained things to us. The place was very clean.. No bugs or Mosquitos.... The buffet food needed improvement as the hot food  was barely warm. However, the staff was very friendly and always smiling. Starky and Ramone were great bartenders... Very attentive... Fun to visit with.

reviews.author: Ryan B
reviews.title: Awesome resort with a phenomenal staff!!!
reviews.text:
I just returned from an awesome stay at The Reserve at Paradisus Punta Cana. Sandra Zorrilla, in member services, did a phenomenal job before we even arrived at the resort. She answered all of our questions, arranged our ground transport, and made our restaurant reservations. She put our minds at ease as this was our first trip to Punta Cana. 

Our arrival at PUJ airport was smooth and we were soo happy Sandra had arranged our travel through blue as we had no hassle at the airport. This can be overwhelming as there are hundreds of taxi vendors waiting. When we arrived at The Reserve, Sandra was waiting to check us in. Check in was quick and our room was ready upon arrival. The villa was very clean and well stocked. Twice daily housekeeping is always a nice surprise!

The entire resort premises is gorgeous! Whether you walk, take the trolley, or ride a bike you are surrounded by tropical well manicured landscape. I was amazed at how attentive the staff were. Even the landscape crew were hospitable. One cut open a coconut and we were able to enjoy fresh count water! Delicious! We loved staying at The Reserve section of the Paradisus. It has a more mature vibe and we found the staff to be extra friendly, accommodating and outgoing here. They had special activities for reserve guests and even had a Reserve Ice Dance Party/Show on Friday nights. The villas are also a great size for families. The pool at the reserve was amazing with in water lounge chairs, cabanas and padded chairs on the pool deck. Emilio Valdez was the pool drink server. He was awesome! Your glass was never empty as he constantly would check in on you and say "time for drinky, drinky!! Woooookay!!!" He was very interactive, engaging and made sure anything we needed was brought right to us. You must try the Emilio special!!

The 2 restaurants at The Reserve, Gabi Cub and Vento, had the best food at the entire resort. They were so accommodating at these restaurants! Janna Ortiz greeted us each morning for breakfast and had the brightest smile. She would always joke with us and designated a table in the restaurant as "ours". Our morning waiter, Antony Cid was a joy as well. As soon as he saw us walk up he had our coffee poured exactly how each of us Iiked it. He was always singing and made us feel right at home. He did his best to answer all our questions and was a fabulous start to each day.

This resort has sooo much activity. You can be as active as you want; however, I highly recommend you get involved and participate in the life enriching activities. It's this group of individuals who make Paradisus Punta Cana so special! Ana and Luis Florian always did an awesome job teaching the dance lessons, but the true star of this group is Rubén Dario Castillos aka the SBB! A truly special and talented individual. Rubén led all the aerobic activities and had a great knowledge about fitness. He had us up, moving and trying new activities so we never had a chance to get bored. From aqua spinning, stretching, cardiobox, aqua gym, candle making, painting, wine pairing, pool parties, he made our trip extra special. He taught us about Dominican heritage, culture, fitness and of course dance! He is the life of the party and we had a blast with him the entire week! Rubén was always patient with us as we practiced our Spanish skills and was there to help translate whenever we needed him. We were able to trust Rubén to create experiences that made this a truly memorable vacation. By the end of the week it felt as if Rubén was part of our familia. We owe Rubén our utmost gratitude for creating an amazing vacation experience!

The only slight misses we had at the resort were with the bike reservation process and building concierge. You must reserve bikes a day in advance and our building concierge were not overly friendly or helpful. You would walk by and they wouldn't always acknowledge you. Asked them to check and see if an early dining time came available for dinner. Their response "you have the late reservation because there was nothing available or they would have booked you an early time"  Thank goodness Sandra had already arranged everything so we didn't have to deal with them. 

Our minimal interaction with the concierge did not spoil our overall experience at this fabulous resort as the Activity Staff and The Reserve Food and Beverage team made up for any lack of hospitality!!! I am sure there are a lot of beautiful resorts in the Dominican Republic but for me it is the PEOPLE that make The Reserve at Paradisus Punta Cana a first class property. I highly recommend this resort as it caters to all types of guests. The staff will do everything they can to ensure you have a remarkable vacation!

reviews.author: Jennifer D
reviews.title: The Reserve ~ Punta Cana
reviews.text: Very nice hotel, excellent pool, very clean, lovely garden, always smiley and positive people serving you. Especially the service by Emilio Valdez at the pool side was more then excellent !!! We stayed at the reserve in room 2431 and enjoyed it a lot, Philippe & Jennifer

reviews.author: CTNicholson
reviews.title: Review for The Reserve at Palma Real
reviews.text:
I would like to acknowledge these people for superior service:  Cristina in  guest services went above and beyond.  What a gem and asset Cristina is!!  Waiters:  Santos and Bolivar were fantastic.  Fransico chef at Aqua is unbelievably talented and service oriented.  Francia in housekeeping was such a hard worker and always had a great smile.  Our wet bar stewart was fantastic (we stayed at The Reserve in building #50 in room 5002).  All the golf cart drivers were great.  The room service staff were fabulous as well.  We had a 1 bedroom master swim up suite and it was great.  The wires for tv's and behind bed  need to be hidden especially for a 5 star resort.  Wifi was terrible in rooms.
Spa was probably the we have ever experienced.  Overall, experience was fantastic.  Todd and Deena of The Woodlands, Texas.

reviews.author: Krismd2014
reviews.title: Wonderful honeymoon
reviews.text: This was our third trip to Paradisus - 7 yrs ago we stayed at the main Paradisus Hotel, the second time we stayed at the Paradisus Reserve - which is about 1/2 a mile from the beach.   Last week we returned to the main Paradisus hotel because we wanted a beach front room for our honeymoon.   Turns out, the only way to get a beachfront room is to upgrade to the Royal Service plan - otherwise you'll be staying in one of the rooms on the interior of the property where there is a massive construction project going on through December.   Royal Service was an expensive upgrade, but we were overall happy we did.   We got a beautiful beachfront room, exclusive access to a high end lounge and the best restaurant on the property, we also had access to a private section on the beach, and a personal butler.    Our butler, Augustin Nuñez, helped us with everything from restaurant reservations, to reserving bali beds on the pool and beach, and even drew us up a romantic jacuzzi bath in our room.   The waitstaff was impeccable - attentive, friendly, and hard-working, and humored me as I practiced my Spanish with them.  In particular Yuderqui Javier was our always friendly and attentive waitress; and Leonardo Mota made excellent Piña Coladas on the beach.  In essence upgrading to Royal Service made our vacation and if you go to the Paradisus we HIGHLY recommend this upgrade.

reviews.author: sagrumpy1962
reviews.title: Unless you have Royal Service expect to be annoyed
reviews.text:
I stayed at the resort 8/9/14 through 8/16/14. I was at the resort with 11 family members (5 rooms). I thought the resort was very nice and well maintained. The rooms were clean, and refrigerator was always stocked. I thought the staff at the resort were very nice and for the most part accommodating. Tipping goes a long way. Luis at the pool bar was great. Beach was beautiful, white fine sand. 

I have been to several all inclusive resorts in Mexico and I felt that the food at the resort was the worst that I have encountered. The breakfast buffet was by far the worst. Eggs were dry, omelettes were hard and everything for the most part was bland. Lunch wasn't much better, they could not even make a descent burger. Cook at the Market Grill at lunch time was absolutely clueless. Nachos and cheese - cheese was ice cold. 

If you haven't booked Royal Service good luck getting a reservation to any of the a la carte restaurants. They tell you they are trying to work out the kinks in the system which is a lie.  You can go on Sunday and attempt to make a reservation on Wednesday. They response is that we will let you know on Wednesday after 4:30. You likely will not get the reservation and if you do it will be at 6:00. So, good luck rounding everyone up and getting ready. What they don't tell you is that the reason for the delay is that they are accommodating the Royal Service guest and if any reservations remain you may get to visit the a la carte restaurants. 

Notice that all of the great reviews are from people who booked Royal Service. The buffet at the time of our visit is set up in the theater. The buffet is actually under renovations and construction goes on day and night. The Royal Service guests have an a la carte restaurant at the pool for breakfast. 

I would also note that at check in no one explained any of the available services or location. I also went to the front desk and asked for a resort map which they had none. The Reserve Resort is on the same access road and you can use their facilities. However to this day, I have no idea what you have access to. No one even explained what services or restaurants you could use at that location.

reviews.author: Stephen G
reviews.title: Great Vacation
reviews.text: We enjoyed a very relaxing and enjoyable 6 days and 5 night stay at the Paradisus Palma Real. We upgraded to the Royal Service package which is a Concierge Butler service. The Person assigned to us was Samuel Rodriguez, who did a very outstanding job. He made our reservations at all the restaurants for diner, transportation back to airport,setting up our double jacuzzi tube in our room to surprise the wife with scented bubble bath with rose peddles sitting on top of the bubbles. They also provide you with a cell phone to reach your Butler through out the day. The shows each night were also very entertaining. They did a production of the Loin King and Michael Jackson that were very good. The bed was awesome the mattress was very comfortable. The hotel staff was very pleasant at all times and helpful. The room itself was excellent.

reviews.author: LaMonica D
reviews.title: Excellent!
reviews.text: I went to the Dominican on Aug 27th - Sept 2nd.  Upon my arrival I read some reviews of this resort. One guy mentioned that he got sick from drinking the water.  Well when I arrived in DR, the guy on the shuttle specifically said to not drink the tap water and he mentioned that the resorts always give bottled water to their guests.  So he was wrong in writing his review.  One other person said that her diamond necklace was stolen off the dresser.  Well mostly all these resorts have safes in the rooms, why not utilize it!  This resort looks exactly like the pictures on the travel websites (expedia, bookit.com, etc).  It was beautiftul!  The people there were nice, very accomodating and attentive.  I want to recognize Angel Araujo, he worked in the area where you get the beach towels, and he was very friendly.  He also teached me a little spanish.  Emmanuel and Miquel that works in the front that help with the suitcases were awesome!  So friendly and attentive.  I will definitely visit this resort again, I had so much fun that I was sad to leave :).  My sister and I already planning to go back next year.

reviews.author: Zuly7360
reviews.title: Excellent service...far and beyond.
reviews.text: Dionisis Martinez, Juan Cabrera, Luis, Anthony, Severino, Ruth and Isabel to name a few of the folks who made this vacation worth while.  There was always a smile, there was always a willingness to serve and please.  Thank you for making this trip unforgettable.  The facility was also very nice and comfortable.

reviews.author: mindy n
reviews.title: SO NICE
reviews.text: Just want to give a shout out for the wonderful service Ramon Ramirez on the Punta Cana Reserve beach gave our family!  He prepared seats, and champagne for a 50th anniversary celebration for my parents.  Then also took photos with our camera so everyone could be in them!  THANK YOU Ramon Ramirez!  Also for the coconut water experience too.

reviews.author: Larissa P
reviews.title: Excelente
reviews.text: Tudo foi perfeito, o atendimento foi maravilhoso com a Anabel, conseguiram fazer a gente se sentir especial como nunca antes em outro hotel, conseguiram reservar o passion, fizeram varias surpresas, foi uma noite inesquecível.

reviews.author: Aline Tatiana G
reviews.title: Hotel incrível!!!!!!
reviews.text:
Nos surpreendeu desde que chegamos, atenção incrível, funcionários prestativos, estão sempre com sorriso no rosto prontos a te atender da melhor forma possível. Nada a reclamar!
Os quartos impecáveis, piscina, comidas, grande variedade sempre, eu não gosto muito de peixes e frutos do mar, eis aí que tinha grande variedades de carne, frango, pastas, hambúrguer, pizza, O que você quiser! 
Os melhores tragos!
Uma dica: Na hora da sua chegada vai ter um ajudante ( o nosso foi Garnier) que vai te dar ajudas com reservas e tal, o melhor e fazer as reservas nos restaurantes logo na chegada esse restaurantes NÃO SÃO PAGOS mais exigem reserva prévia, eu adorei o Grill, servem uma picanha a moda brasileira deliciosa! O buffet funciona todos os dias, as vezes e preciso pegar um carinho de golf que pasa cada 5 min e ir até o Gabi Club no The Reserve.
Eles nos ofereceram na chegada o Royal Service, mais achei um pouco carinho 600$ por pessoa. Não recomendo! Porque você desfruta de tuuudooo e não sente falta desse serviço, que não te da tantas vantagens assim. Você não se priva de nada, só de uma piscina mais pequena.. Enfim..
Tem atividades todas as noites, muitos shows, vale a pena conferir!
Amamos tudo e se voltar pretendo que seja nesse hotel! Não creio que os outros sejam tão bons!

reviews.author: MikeJenvey
reviews.title: Very nice property - but construction in progress
reviews.text:
PARADISUS SPA & GOLF RESORT, PALMA REAL, PUNTA CANA

[IMPORTANT NOTE – THERE IS CONSTRUCTION WORK AT THE HOTEL – PLEASE READ BELOW & CHECK WITH YOUR TRAVEL COMPANY – OURS WAS NOT AWARE]

This is our 5th Caribbean “all-inclusive” holiday, our first time to the Dominican Republic (DR).  We are a family group, with 2 children (daughter aged 19, son almost 17).  We stayed from Aug 2014 into early Sep. This is a long review, but if you are spending a significant budget on a holiday, it’s worth knowing what you get!

Punta Cana Airport – on arrival, the immigration was quick & efficient.  Useful to obtain the mandatory tourist cards (GBP10 each) in advance via the DR Embassy in London; it saves an element of queuing to get past the tourist card desk before immigration.  No baggage trollies can be taken from the last point in the arrivals hall, but there are porters if you travel with a mountain of suitcases! Check-in for departure was efficient.  You will need to complete an immigration card, similar to the inbound form, before going through security screening.   In the first section of departure, was the first area of duty-free & tourist souvenir shopping.  Further around was the food hall – “Little America” with Wendys & Cinnabon!  Continuing to Gates 6-10, there is a more modern section, (much cooler) again with duty-free shopping, VIP lounge (Priority Pass accepted; bother, didn’t bring my card!) & a pharmacy.

Resort location – via a drop-off at 2 locations (both at nearby Barcelo resort), the transfer took 30 mins.  Our transfer was in a large coach rather than the expected mini-bus; we met the relevant tour representative outside the arrivals part of the terminal.  Note that there is a Paradisus Reserve & Royal Service;  the Reserve (separate hotel) takes up a large part of the overall resort.

Check-in – the main “lobby” area is much bigger than we have encountered in other resorts; it certainly had a grandiose feeling to it.  We had a hiccup with our rooms at first; both on our reservation & a follow-up email, we had requested our 2 rooms (Garden View Suites) to be in close proximity.  The initial allocation was for rooms in separate buildings.  After some to-ing & fro-ing at reception, we went to one room pending a check on availability.  After waiting in the room for about 30 mins, we were advised that we then had 2 rooms, next door to each other (1055/1057 – ground floor in 3 floor block – about 250m away from main building).  You will get “tagged” with a bracelet with the colour matching your guest “status.”  Expect to be introduced to a concierge who will try to be your “personal” contact for your holiday, to help with minor issues or make restaurant reservations.  Ours was Franklin (the one with the hair!) & he was very helpful during our stay.

Check-out – normal time is 1200 hrs.  Our rep advised to leave the hotel at least 3 hrs before airline departure time.  We asked for a one hr extension to our check-out time which was approved (we probably could have got even longer on the day), so we vacated our rooms, chilled in the Lobby Bar for while, went to lunch, then got our transfer at 1455 hrs (for 1800 hrs flight).  We had to leave our bracelets when leaving, in exchange for a “check-out” form.  This was required on boarding our transfer bus, no idea what the principle was.  Again, we went via Barcelo resort on the way to the airport.

Rooms – compared with other resorts, they certainly had a “wow” factor.  The dimensions were great – from entrance lobby wall to window was about 12m.  The furnishings were of high quality & well laid out.  Our super-king bed was probably a bit larger than the UK standard & extremely comfortable to sleep in.  The (large) bathroom had a big jacuzzi bath, separate toilet & separate (large – room for 2) shower with massage jets.  There was a separate small wardrobe “room,” just large enough for suitcases & one (small) area for hanging clothes up – only about 2 feet of hanging rail, not really enough (much better space in our kids’ room).  The far end of the room nearest to the window was a “lounge” area with outside balcony.  Curtains were of a good “black-out” type, no light was let in.  The air conditioning was the modern “pipe” system (rather than a wall-mounted unit) & was very quiet & efficient.  There was a good-sized room safe in the wardrobe room.  The electrical power points were USA-style twin flat-pin – useful tip – bring a UK mini-extension lead device (4 power sockets); then you only need one USA adaptor to plug in the main plug of the extension to give you 4 UK sockets.   Our children had a similar room – their main concern for privacy was that the bathroom area was very open, with part-frosted shower/toilet doors & slatted (fixed) shutters that could be opened/closed to partially separate the bathroom from the bedroom area – but there were 2 relatively open areas at each end of the shutters. We had some niggles – the shower in our room wouldn’t drain properly, but that was fixed the next day, & there was a “movement sensor” that would ensure that the lights, air etc, would stay on.  Ours was not sensitive enough (or the main power switch by the bed was faulty), so the main lights would go off every 10 mins or so; this fixed by the end of our 3rd day.  The re-stocking of the (free) ‘fridges in both our rooms seemed haphazard over several days, but as with room cleaning staff, the Do Not Disturb (DnD) sign was no barrier!  For 5 days in a row, after the rooms had been cleaned, we had to ask for shampoos to be delivered to the kids’ room.  Not sure of the reason (clean towels?), but the room maid would also be knocking on doors at 1845 hrs in the evening.  There is a “bed turn-down” service if you leave the DnD sign off. 

Room cleaning – in our building, the cleaning maids were knocking on doors at 0845!  Make sure you put the “DnD” sign on the door with the lettering facing outwards – the reverse side was blank, & didn’t seem to indicate that peace was required…..  And, even with the lettering facing outwards, this didn’t stop ‘em!  Indeed, one morning between 0930 & 1005 hrs (I was in bed, dozing, not feeling too well with a tummy bug), I got 2 attempts from the mini-bar staff AND a ‘phone call to ask me that as the DnD sign was on the door, what time did I want the room cleaned??!! Grrr!!!!  That said, the standard of cleaning was very good.  For both our rooms, we had to ask far too many times for shower gels, etc.  As the maids didn’t speak much English, we always had to go through Guest Services = too much extra time.

Tour representative – as part of our check-in paperwork, we were given an “invitation” to meet up with the holiday representative at 1400 hrs the next day.  We waited in the general area near Guest Services, but didn’t see anyone.  It turned out that the representative had a separate desk downstairs (ground level) where you can book excursions or tours;  it wasn’t the “standard” welcome meeting that we have experienced elsewhere.  It was, however, the point of contact for the holiday company (Trailfinders for us) in the event of any formal complaint, etc.

Currency – contrary to the wrong advice (that we ignored!) from our local M&S exchange bureau, as with all other place we have visited in the Caribbean, US $$ = main tourist currency.  Taxi to the airport = US $30.

Resort “discount” vouchers – just next to the entrance to Market Grill, there is a desk where you can get a booklet of vouchers towards certain items within the resort, such as non-standard wines, Spa treatments, etc.

Restaurants – 4 major options, Olympus, Market Grill, Passion, Venta & Bana.  Note that for Passion & Venta = “elegant” dress code (“Resort Elegant” is defined incorrectly on the Melia website; it should be “sleeved shirt” not “long-sleeved shirt” & long trousers for men + “closed toe” shoes, not tennis shoes).  Aqua = in Reserve Hotel (within the “all inclusive” aspects, also “elegant” dress code).  All restaurants had very nice house white wine.  High chairs are available.  No Earl Grey tea though! As with all such resorts, there is a booking system in place.  Unusually, we didn’t have any “pre-reservation” made by the hotel for the evening of our arrival.  You may wish to email ahead a preference – from our inbound BA flight, we arrived at reception at about 1930 hrs, so to allow for check-in administration, etc, the earliest suggested time would be 2030-2100 hrs?  However, this is by no means guaranteed to work!  

Restaurant Booking system - we had huge difficulties in getting timings/locations to our preferred choice; you had to leave the details with the Guest Service desk (or your concierge) & then get confirmation at about 1630 hrs – this was normally by note delivered to the room; on one evening, this arrived at 1755 hrs!  This was very poor, as it didn’t allow the flexibility to know the confirmed timings/location before you set off for the day – especially if you went on a day’s excursion, or decided to have a late lunch – ah, only available dinner reservation time is 1800 hrs (as we had)!  It was a very backward system, as Guest Services did not have any input into the bookings other than to email them or ‘phone them through to the restaurant booking “centre.”  They also could not tell you in advance if your preferred restaurant/timing is unavailable & suggest an alternative; it made it a stressful experience.  Of course, if you couldn’t get a reservation, you had the Olympus buffet option, but that isn’t why people chose an all-inclusive resort.  It shouldn’t be necessary to liaise with the Food & Beverage (F&B) manager in order to get preferred times – goodness knows what it was like when the hotel was much busier.  There were a couple of F&B-specific concierges that move between the different restaurants.  We chatted to one USA family who would not return if the booking system stayed the same.

[NOTE – met with the F&B manager, Charles.  He explained the limitations of the current system – Guest Services desk cannot make direct entry into the reservations system or see “live” booking status, & not enough staff to take calls by ‘phone direct to the Dinner Reservations department (ext 8005, opens at 0900 hrs).  Work is in progress to improve the software & perhaps “split” the booking options into 2 (or more) desks with “live” viewing options so that if the first choice isn’t available, then other options can be chosen immediately.  The replacement restaurant for the burnt-out one should open 01 Nov 2014.  Currently, the intention is to serve buffet lunch, but with separated food stations (like mini-kitchens) so that there can be ‘demonstration” cuisine in the evenings; the evening use would also have the restaurant split into 2, so that one part would be buffet, the other “a la carte.”  One “wing” of the new facility would possibly be for family accommodation rooms, perhaps with a separate “family” restaurant.]

Olympus – this is the largest restaurant.  Due to a fire some months ago (firework let off at a wedding reception!), this was located in the theatre/ballroom.  The fire also damaged a major aerial for the internet in the area.  Breakfast was served there with a good range of items, but no option for eggs/omelettes to order.  We had dinner (buffet) there on the first night; mixed reviews from my family group.  The salad & fruit items were very good, but the main courses didn’t fit in with some of our tastes so much.  Mon nights were “DR Theme Night” with local food choices & a variety of local crafts for sale. Some of the food displays were really works of art;  presentation was superb in some areas.

[NOTE – on 01 Sep, breakfast & lunch was no longer served in Olympus, those meals moved to the Chinese Fusion area in Bana; at lunch, option to have pieces or meat/fish, or prawns, cooked to order in the Teppanyaki part.]

[NOTE – low season – from 02 Sep, some restaurants close alternately in the evening.  Market Grill & Teppanyaki closed for the first evening that we encountered this.

[NOTE - Olympus “replacement” – due to the fire, there is a large-scale building project in progress; this is clearly visible from the main pool area & there was some significant associated construction noise.]

Market Grill – this is open air, facing the beach (& the private pool for the Reserve guests).  Breakfast was served there with a good range of items; you could also get eggs/omelettes cooked to order – the omelette chef was the busiest man of the resort at breakfast, quite often there was a long queue.   For lunch, expect a few hot dishes, or burgers + fries, stir-grilled chicken with sliced vegetables for fajitas, or paella.  Dinner = steaks, choice of burger, fish, etc, all nicely cooked.  

Venta – Mediterranean – nice service, a little more “up market” than the other restaurants. If you have teenagers who don’t really have a taste for “fancy cuisine,” this isn’t the place.  The portion sizes were much smaller than at Bana.

Bana – this is described as “Asian Fusion & is split into 3 areas, a sushi bar, Teppanyaki tables (food cooked in front of you) & a “Chinese Fusion” restaurant.  We ate in the  Chinese area 2 nights in a row – slightly disappointing, the menu was the same, not even a “dish of the day” option (this was mentioned to F&B manager). Food was of good quality, but the main course were huge portions, probably twice the size of a serving in a restaurant elsewhere.  The chicken Schezuan was advertised as spicy (2* with 3* being the hottest), but it was very bland.  The Teppanyaki “cook in front of you” experience was good fun, we ate there twice – we sat as a total of 12 people around the cook’s station.  As with the Chinese food, the portions were huge – choice of 2 items from the menu (beef, chicken, salmon & prawns) – very tasty food overall.  If the chef is being entertaining, be prepared to catch tofu in your mouth! Sushi experience – superb food, no other way to describe it.  

Passion (adults only) – supplement to pay.  Due to one family member being under the age of 18, we did not use this restaurant.

Aqua – located at the Reserve Hotel within the resort – Italian/Mediterranean theme, very nice decoration & atmosphere.  Great food, a choice of 7 starters (including 2 hot soups), 4 pasta & risotto dishes, 3 fish (including salmon – a huge fillet), & 3 meat courses.  The beef steak was very, very tender;  all the mains came with very small portions of accompanying “trimmings.”  Desserts were also to a high standard.  

Agave – Mexican – not available due to the fire.  This was not mentioned on Melia website.

Naos – “pool-side” - not available due to the fire.  This was not mentioned on Melia website.

Hotel population – other than walking to our room on the first night, there were very few UK guests – so thankfully few tattoo displays!  The guests seemed to be made up of mainly Americans & Spanish-speaking people (no idea if they were from USA or other countries).  Someone from the USA told us that earlier in the month of Aug, the hotel was normally pretty full, with large queues & (even more) difficulties getting restaurant bookings, etc.  Quite cheap prices from USA to DR via JetBlue (equivalent of easyJet), etc.

Language – some of the staff spoke excellent English, but their work position didn’t always reflect their ability.  We had occasional difficulty throughout our stay, but for example, at the “Club House” (collect towels for the pool), a couple of the guys spoke much better English, almost to colloquial standard – Angel was very helpful.  We found one of them also working an evening shift in one of the restaurants.

Wheelchair access – as far as we could see, all major areas & ground floor rooms were wheelchair accessible.  No idea if there are rooms that have any special adaptions or wider doors, etc.  We didn’t see any ramps for pool access, but the steps into the water have a fairly shallow graduation, i.e. not steep.  At one end (nearest Market Grill), the “steps” were about one yard “long” so perhaps the easiest point of access for anyone with mobility issues.

Pool – There was one very large pool (largest we have seen in a hotel), with separate “jacuzzi” hydro-massage areas, & built-in “loungers” in the water, some with shade.  NO lifeguard – the pool is a constant 4.75 foot depth – younger children would have to be closely monitored; there is a separate (very small) kids’ pool.  The water was always clean with no noticeable chlorine sting to the eyes. Around the pool area, there were numerous “fixed” sun shades that were quite large (you could get 4 sunbeds underneath), & well “roofed” with palm leafs, so all completely protected below from any rain showers, & also separate “bed” areas.  Our concierge advised that it was quite normal to “reserve” your location by placing towels, etc, on the sunbeds.  There was a drinks/snacks bar where you can also sit in the water.  Water in bottles = good! Premium alcohol was available (Beefeater, VAT69, etc) for those on the harder stuff. Staff walk by & you can ask them for drinks – if they don’t ask you first.  Drinks from the pool bar were served in paper cups = no safety hazards around or in the pool.  Not easy to get milkshakes sometimes.  Towels are available from 0800 hrs from the “Club House” – a separate hut just to the rear of the pool area, past the bar.  At the Club House, there is a small storage area for books (to exchange) – but a distinct lack of books – I left 10!  [It is suggested that a separate “library” is established indoors, so that guests can swap or leave books.  Very, very limited options to buy books at the hotel shops or locally - & about US $10 for a nondescript title – take them with you.] Several restrooms around the pool, all spotlessly clean & checked regularly (same for the restrooms throughout the hotel).  

Pool bust up - one morning, a large group of guests decided that it was appropriate to play party music at the pool, very loud; we did not pay to come to Benidorm!  It took 4-5 visits from staff to get them to stop doing this – the member of staff would leave, then the music would be turned up to loud volume again; this went on for a couple of hours. We went to visit the mall to get away from the noise, with the stated requirement that it was either stop the noise, or, upgrade us to Royal Suite status so we could use alternative facilities.  When we returned from the mall, the proposed solution was for us to use the Royal Suite access at the far end of the pool; this proved to be successful.  However, from what we could see over our last few days, this seemed to be where other non-Royal Suite guests also hid away!  Apparently, in high season, a member of staff is stationed by the entrance to stop interlopers.  Follow-up – the noisy group continued to be disruptive, wanted to change the “background” music that plays all around the pool (to use their own), got into a fight with security personnel, & were told that they had to leave the hotel!  There was another fight later on in the lobby when they checked out!!  Note that this is not typical of the other hotel guests – in fact, in all our holidays, we have never encountered such goings-on.

{NOTE – until 01 Nov (scheduled opening of new restaurant, etc), there is a large construction eyesore at the far end of the pool, adjacent to the hydro-massage pools.  There was associated noise, including jack hammers at times – even at 1930 hrs one evening whilst we were waiting to eat at the Market Grill, & at 1045 hrs at breakfast.  This was (& at time of submitting this) not advertised on the Melia website, nor was it notified to us when we booked our holiday – from feedback so far, it was not known to the product department for our holiday company, Trailfinders.]

Room service – other than alcohol & some specialist items, the 24 hr room service menu was within the “all inclusive” & offered a good choice of menu items.  The range of items is limited between 2300 hrs – 0700 hrs or thereabouts.

Beach – it was a fantastic white sand & clean sea to swim in.  Similar large sun shades as with the main pool, but of course, popular with hotel guests.  However, on several days, possibly due to strong winds, there were large deposits on seaweed in the water by the edge of the beach.  There seemed to be a clean-up plan, as after a couple of days, it had all disappeared, but some did return.

Water-sports – representatives from the banana boat/para-sail “Scuba” company walk up & down by the pool each day, so stop one for details & prices.  Two people for the banana boat = US $30 – original asking price $40.  Note that the boat does NOT pick up at Paradisus – it was necessary to walk about half a mile!  The Paradisus does not have kayaks, mini-catamarans or snorkeling kit.

Gymnasium – this had a very good range of modern equipment.  For children under 18, you need to sign a waiver for damages/injuries, etc.  Arrange this via Guest Services or your concierge.

Entertainment – there was a variety of evening music, in the main “central” area.  For one evening, held in the Olympus restaurant/theatre, there was a local version of “Stomp” which was pretty good.  The “Lion King” was also entertaining, especially for the younger kids.  Best of all was the Michael Jackson tribute show – brilliant look-alike, with all the moves.  As all the accommodation is some distance away from the entertainment area, there were no noise issues that we have experienced at smaller resorts.  There is a free shuttle bus at 2300 hrs to a local disco; entry fee $15, cost of drinks unknown, time of return shuttle unknown! 

Internet – there were several usable (free) networks, “Paradisus,” “Reserve Internet Access” & “Palma Real.”  Due to one major aerial damaged (on top of restaurant that was burnt out), there were areas where coverage was sketchy.  However, coverage in the rooms seemed to work one day, but not the next; 2 networks always seemed to stop working completely in the rooms during late evening into the next morning.  There is work in progress for network + infrastructure improvement.  Whilst not a prime factor in our choice of holiday location, with 2 children, it was an important consideration (& good to check on excursions, etc), so it was frustrating to have an advertised facility that was sub-optimal.  On the 7th evening, we were (finally) told that there should be a functional wi-fi router in each room; ours had no power cable.  These were checked & powered up, & initially seemed to work.  However, in the evening, there was no network connection again, so Days 7 - 10, still no internet in the room, & this remained the situation until we left, despite attempts to fix it; all very disappointing.  We had been advised by email from the hotel before we arrived that internet would be available in the rooms.

Gardens – these are extremely well laid out, & look very good.  There were always gardeners out & about tidying up, etc.  Apparently, across the resort, there are about 1000 employees just for the gardens!  There was a separate garden “courtyard” with fountain in our building, very pretty indeed - & the fountain was on a timer, so switched off at night. Look at for the flamingos in their own pool! Expect to see a wedding set-up somewhere on your stay.

Tour of “Paradisus Reserve” – expect your concierge to offer you the chance of touring the Reserve for a 90 minute presentation; it seems that this is part of their work/salary requirement.  This was a sales opportunity if you want to become a member of the Melia Members Club.  It’s not time-share, but still a money-making opportunity for the hotel group – you buy “points” that allow you preferential rates & no “black-out” dates; a 4 person double suite would typically cost US $110-$150 per day instead of full price.  The suite we viewed was of exceptional quality, twin beds in one area, separate lounge, then further bedroom suite, either with private pool (ground floor) or 2 separate Jacuzzi baths on the balcony areas.  To buy 88,000 points for 2 weeks each year at a hotel of the same quality as Paradisus (world-wide options), a mere US $59,500 – just under GBP36K!  This would effectively be valid for 25 yrs.  There was a cheaper option for one week, with a 15% deposit, 20% in the next 60 days, & the balance over 2 years (interest free credit – how generous!).  We declined, but got “rewarded” with 2 x US $45 vouchers for 2 people using local excursion options provided by “City Tour” (never worked out how to use them) & also 30,000 loyalty points towards the Melia hotel loyalty card.

Shops + Mall – there were couple of very good shops below the lobby area.  Also, with a free shuttle bus (every 15 mins), you can get to a Mall that is located just by the main entrance to the resort; unless you were after some designer items, not really worth the visit.  There is an Outback steak restaurant & some other food outlets (not experienced).  Separate visit (arranged via holiday rep) – about 10 mins (free) drive to a small cigar outlet, where you can see how local cigars are made, & of course buy some, then onwards to a small local chocolate outlet.  The chocolate tea (yes, really – made from the husks of the cocoa beans!) was quite nice.  Of course, these outlets are tacked onto larger gift shops with other tourist items for sale.  These 2 visits + transport took just under 2 hrs.

Excursion – as always, lots on offer from the different reps.  We chose the Marinium  “swim with sharks + rays” experience, US $99 each.  After the transfer (25 mins to the south east side corner of the island), it consisted of a short boat ride to 2 enclosed areas, where you firstly swam (snorkel + mask) with sharks & stingrays for about 40 mins, then moved to the next large “pen.”  Yes, you are in the same area as the (nanny) sharks & the rays but they all stay on the bottom, well away from the people intruders.  We were spoiled in Antigua where the swim with stingrays was a real “wow” total experience, where you fed the rays & they swam round you, between people & through your legs.  The next enclosure was with some other rays (& a couple of isolated sharks), with a photo opportunity to have your picture taken holding a stingray; cost of a photo was US $15.  After the swim/snorkeling, the boat went along the coast & drinks + snacks were served; if you take the afternoon trip, have lunch before you go, the snacks were very small.  Take ear plugs if you don’t like loud music – we had wanted a quieter tour.  A stop was made for about 40 mins at a “natural pool” in the sea, & then we returned – although there seemed to have been engine issues, as we were drifting near to the coast for about 15 mins.    This ‘experience” was very mundane & to us, not what we were after.  

Mosquitos/Malaria prevention – all the UK medical/travel advice stated that this area of the DR was “medium” risk from mosquitos, so it was recommended to take malaria tablets.  We sourced ours (“Avioclor”) from our local Lloyds pharmacy (no prescription required), & for 3 boxes, this cost us just over £26.00.  The requirement is to take 2 tablets with food, one week before departure, & then 2 further tablets weekly on the same day of the week, to continue until the 4th week after travel back home.  Compared to other resorts we have been to, we did not see a single mosquito, either outside or in our rooms.  Your choice – you might find insect repellent & suitable clothes in the evening to be a better option.  Also, very few ants, no flies or other nasty insects!

Medical – the nearest facility is the Hospiten Bavaro (+1 809 686 1414), 24 hr emergency department, with dentist & family GP available; prices for consultations, etc, unknown. (Punta Cana, Cta Higuey, 500m Cruce de Veron, Bavaro.)

Summary – great resort potential, luxury product in many areas, very clean, & with very friendly/helpful staff.  The main areas & rooms were to a very high standard.  For us, our holiday was let down by the construction work with associated noise & the vagaries of the restaurant booking difficulties.  The unpredictability & eventual demise of the internet in our rooms was also frustrating.

reviews.author: Cheryl B
reviews.title: Not at all happy with the Royal Service
reviews.text: The royal service was bad. We didn't see our so called butler Juan for the first 24 hours. When we did see him, all he could say was call him(our phone didn't work). We would only se him every 24 hours and it was four days before he could call us by name. Our shower  did not work right for the last the last four days. We told Juan and about four other people, and it was NEVER fixed. The royal service bar was terrible, we have to go to the swim up bar to get any service. Getting a drink on the beach was bad, we ended up getting our drinks at the swim up bar, they were better and twice as fast. The place was far under staffed. Nice place to stay do not get the Royal Service!!

reviews.author: GLGorman
reviews.title: The return was just as wonderful!
reviews.text: I took my daughters to The Reserve at Paradisus Punta Cana last summer and the vacation was so terrific, we decided to return this August (and took a dear friend who was experiencing his first trip out of the country).  It seems unbelievable but there were employees that remembered us from a year ago!  Once again, we had the most wonderful time.  The room was spacious and clean.  There was a wide variety of great food, even satisfying two vegetarians and a body-builder.  We went to the gym every day and it is well equipped.  The single best feature of the resort, however, is the staff!  We had outstanding service on the beach from Ramon Ramirez, Luis Santana and Jorge Elena.  I can't say enough about the hardworking people in the Gabi Reserve Restaurant including Celso Peralta and Robert Jorge.  Also, huge appreciation for the men that made our delicious omelets every morning - great job!  Finally, a huge shout-out to the superior gym staff: Ricardo Vasquez, Nelson Hidalgo, Manuel Cespedes and Rafael.  There are a lot of resorts that have beautiful rooms, gorgeous beaches, and terrific food but, we would go back to this one for the people!

reviews.author: Phyllis G
reviews.title: In Paradise
reviews.text: Alvaro Fernandez our butler took care of our every need, and was instrumental in changing our accommodations, as well as making our dinner reservations, and pointing out places of interest. Leonardo Mota served up the warmest smile with his sensational pina coladas.The best we had ever tasted. The trips to his station in the outdoor bar became a great joy to myself and my fiancee. Lucilia and Marias' wonderful ability to perform massages on the beach were truly an experience we will never forget. But the most important member of the team was the lead off hitter the sensational Natalia Green. Natalia was the first staff member we encountered and she was wonderful. I would be remiss in my assessment if I failed to mention the wonderful treatment we received from the Ladies working in the Oriental Garden Spa. The massages we received from these lovely Philippines young ladies was so great we didn't want to get up when the massage was over.!  Overall the Paradisus Royal Service experience was awesome and we hope to one day return!!!!

reviews.author: Jvoss14
reviews.title: Wonderful stay for our honeymoon, couldn't have asked for more
reviews.text: The hotel and amenities were wonderful;the royal service upgrade is well worth it, our butler Juan de Leon truly made our experience as wonderful as possible. Highly recommend this resort, wonderful food and time.

reviews.author: Mvoss830
reviews.title: Excellent honeymoon!
reviews.text: Our honeymoon experience at Paradisus Palma Real was superb. Upgrading to Royal Service is well worth it! Our butler Juan De Lion was excellent and went above and beyond to make us feel welcome and cared for. We will definitely be coming back!

reviews.author: Anne M
reviews.title: Iydillic Setting
reviews.text:
We had a wonderful stay at the El Paradisus Palma Real Punta Cana.
Doing the Royal Service was the right thing to do as it gave us access to all the restaurants  and enjoyed the private beach and pools.  The food in all the restaurants were of high quality, tasty, well presented.  The house wine was very good and plentiful.
